ABF build-up film should be treated as an upstream substrate-material gate; evidence confirms ABF is used in high-performance semiconductor package substrates, but current allocation tightness needs further verification.
AI-server MLCCs and power modules are emerging second-order bottleneck nodes; Murata explicitly cited increased server capacitors and power-supply modules in its April 30, 2026 forecast.
Data-center electrical distribution and behind-the-meter power should be tracked as physical deployment bottlenecks; Powell's fiscal Q2 2026 results provide order and backlog evidence.

Semiconductor equipment subsystems, contamination control, specialty chemistry, and cleaning services remain underfollowed nodes that may capture value from advanced-node and advanced-packaging capacity expansion.
Compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools are a hypothesis node tied to AI optical connectivity; verify through order intake, customer commentary, and laser/InP/GaAs capacity signals.

summary: Split Layer 2 synthesis. Initial Layer 2A industry-chain map for the broad Technology theme, narrowed by current evidence toward AI infrastructure physical bottlenecks rather than headline AI chip leaders. The most Serenity-relevant nodes are not the high-attention GPU/cloud platform layer, but upstream and adjacent choke points: high-end IC package substrates, ABF build-up film, AI-server MLCCs and power components, medium-voltage electrical distribution, behind-the-meter power, semiconductor equipment subsystems, contamination-control services, compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools for optics, and certification/qualification gates. This is an industry-chain and catalyst map only, not a security recommendation.

supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Large AI training and inference clusters drive demand for accelerators, HBM, optical links, AI servers, data-center shells, power, cooling, and upstream component capacity. This is the visible demand driver, but not necessarily the best bottleneck node because it is highly watched.

supply_chain_map.node: AI accelerator and custom ASIC programs
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Accelerator launches determine substrate complexity, HBM stack demand, board-level power density, capacitor counts, and optical interconnect requirements. The node is high-attention and should be used mainly as the demand reference point for lower-attention suppliers.

AI accelerators are increasingly memory-bandwidth constrained, making HBM supply and packaging capacity critical. However, this node is already crowded in market attention, so the funnel should look one layer deeper into substrates, tools, materials, and process-control inputs.

supply_chain_map.node: High-end IC package substrates for AI servers
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Advanced AI packages require larger, more complex substrates with tighter features and higher yield requirements. Capacity additions require heavy capex, long qualification, customer coordination, and yield learning, making this one of the clearest physical bottleneck candidates.

supply_chain_map.node: ABF build-up film and substrate insulation materials
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: ABF film is a key material for high-performance semiconductor package substrates. If substrate capacity expands faster than qualified material supply, ABF allocation can become a hidden upstream gate below the substrate makers.

supply_chain_map.node: AI-server MLCCs and high-reliability passive components
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: AI servers and accelerator boards require many more capacitors and stricter electrical performance than ordinary servers. The bottleneck is not generic MLCC volume, but high-capacitance, low-ESR, low-ESL, high-reliability parts qualified for dense AI-server power delivery.

supply_chain_map.node: AI-server power modules and board-level power delivery
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Higher accelerator power draw increases demand for voltage regulation, power modules, low-impedance capacitor networks, connectors, busbars, and thermal-aware board design. This node can hide component suppliers that are less followed than GPU or server OEM names.

supply_chain_map.node: Medium-voltage switchgear, electrical distribution, and control systems
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Large data centers need engineered electrical systems, switchgear, protection, control, and distribution equipment. Backlogs and large data-center orders suggest physical electrical infrastructure is becoming a measurable AI-capex pass-through.

supply_chain_map.node: Behind-the-meter generation and data-center power architecture
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Grid interconnection timelines and power availability can constrain AI cluster deployment. Behind-the-meter generation, microgrids, and on-site power designs are emerging as ways to secure capacity, creating bottlenecks in engineering, equipment, permitting, and gas/power interconnects.

supply_chain_map.node: Grid interconnection, utility upgrades, and permitting
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Even when compute equipment is available, data-center energization can be delayed by utility queue times, transmission constraints, substation equipment, environmental approvals, and local permitting. This regulated gate can redirect value toward electrical contractors, grid equipment, and power-development assets.

supply_chain_map.node: Liquid cooling, cold plates, CDUs, pumps, and thermal interfaces
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Rack power density growth increases the need for liquid cooling and thermal management. The bottleneck may sit in qualified cooling components, integration know-how, leak reliability, and data-center retrofit capability rather than in commodity cooling hardware.

supply_chain_map.node: Optical interconnect modules and silicon photonics
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Cluster scale increases bandwidth demand between accelerators, racks, and data halls. Optical modules are visible, but the more interesting lower-attention nodes may be lasers, compound-semiconductor wafers, epitaxy tools, optical test, packaging, and high-speed connectors.

supply_chain_map.node: Compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools for lasers and optical devices
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: AI optical connectivity ultimately depends on laser and photonic device manufacturing capacity. Epitaxy equipment sits upstream of modules and can become a hidden tool-layer bottleneck if InP/GaAs laser demand accelerates.

supply_chain_map.node: Semiconductor equipment gas, liquid, vacuum, RF power, and process-control subsystems
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Advanced-node fabs and packaging capacity rely on qualified subsystems embedded inside larger OEM tools. These suppliers are often classified as industrial or component manufacturers, making them underfollowed relative to front-end equipment leaders.

supply_chain_map.node: Ultra-high-purity cleaning, contamination control, filtration, and specialty chemicals
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: As feature sizes shrink and advanced packaging complexity rises, contamination tolerance falls. Qualified cleaning, filtration, purification, CMP consumables, and specialty chemical suppliers can become recurring bottleneck nodes with long qualification cycles.

supply_chain_map.node: Advanced packaging OSAT capacity and yield learning
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: CoWoS-like advanced packaging, interposers, substrate attach, and final test capacity can limit shipment timing. This node is high-attention, but related second-order inputs such as substrates, ABF, plating chemistry, test sockets, and cleaning may be less efficiently priced.

supply_chain_map.node: Specialty plating chemistry and substrate manufacturing consumables
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Advanced substrates and packaging require specialized plating, wet chemistry, and process consumables. This node can hide value in diversified materials companies that do not screen cleanly as AI beneficiaries.

supply_chain_map.node: Distributor and allocation channels for high-end electronics components
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: When passive components, power components, and specialty parts tighten, authorized distributors and allocation relationships can determine which server and board manufacturers receive supply first. This is a low-attention node that should be checked for inventory, book-to-bill, and lead-time signals.

supply_chain_map.node: Customer qualification, reliability certification, and design-in cycles
supply_chain_map.why_it_matters: Many AI infrastructure inputs cannot be swapped quickly once qualified into accelerators, servers, power systems, or semiconductor tools. Long design-in and reliability cycles create supplier lock-in and make apparent commodity nodes behave like bottlenecks.
